DADGAD.desc: Modal "Celtic" tuning — the open strings ring a Dsus4. Pioneered by Davey Graham.
DADGAD.song: "She Moved Through the Fair" — Davey Graham

Nashville.desc: "High-strung" — the lower four strings swap to light gauges an octave up for a shimmering, 12-string-like chime. A studio doubling trick.

Baritone.desc: A long-scale guitar tuned a fourth low (B to B); born in surf and spaghetti-western scores.

Bass VI.desc: The whole guitar dropped a full octave — the Fender Bass VI's baritone-bass register, between guitar and bass.

Hendrix.desc: Standard tuned down a half step to E♭ — slinkier strings and a darker, fatter tone. Jimi's default.

C6.desc: The workhorse sixth-chord lap-steel tuning — rich western-swing, jazz and Hawaiian voicings (Jerry Byrd's C6).
C6.song: "Steel Guitar Rag" — Bob Wills & His Texas Playboys

A6.desc: C6 transposed down a minor third for a warmer, lower western-swing voice (Herb Remington, Leon McAuliffe).

C6/A7.desc: A Jerry-Byrd-style hybrid giving both a C6 and an A7 in one tuning, for Hawaiian and country lap steel.
C6/A7.song: Hawaiian & country lap steel — Jerry Byrd

E7.desc: A sevenths tuning — bluesy, dominant colour favoured for blues and rock slide (layout varies).
E7.song: early Hawaiian & blues lap steel — Sol Hoʻopiʻi

E13.desc: A rich extended-chord tuning for western swing and jazz lap steel (the McAuliffe/Remington era).
E13.song: western swing — Bob Wills & His Texas Playboys

E9 lap.desc: Lush E-major-9 voicings for non-pedal lap steel — the non-pedal cousin of the country pedal-steel E9.

B11.desc: A gorgeous, quintessentially Hawaiian lap-steel tuning full of extended chords; also half of Don Helms' Hank Williams double-neck (E6/B11).
B11.song: Hank Williams sides (Don Helms) — e.g. "Your Cheatin' Heart"

Cyrus Hybrid.desc: A specialised hybrid voicing — the open strings spell a Gmaj9.

Open E.desc: An open E-major chord — the classic bottleneck-slide tuning.
Open E.song: "Statesboro Blues" — The Allman Brothers Band (Duane Allman)

Open D.desc: Open D major ("Vestapol") — a cornerstone of Delta blues and folk fingerstyle/slide.

Open G Dobro.desc: The standard resonator/Dobro tuning — the sound of bluegrass and Hawaiian-style slide.

Open G low.desc: Full six-string open G — the classic Delta-blues "Spanish" tuning and the basis of the Stones' open-G sound.

Open A high.desc: Open A major — open G raised a whole step for a brighter, tenser slide tone, with the same chord shapes. The higher-voiced counterpart to open G.

Drop D.desc: The low string dropped a whole step for one-finger power chords and a heavier low end.

Drop Db.desc: Drop D shifted down a half step (Drop C#) for extra weight while staying playable.

Drop C.desc: Drop D down a whole step — a huge nu-metal/metalcore rhythm tuning.

Drop B.desc: Drop D down a minor third — heavy, tight and modern.

Drop Bb.desc: Drop D down a fourth (Drop A#) for a crushing low register.

Drop A.desc: The low string down a fourth then dropped — a metalcore/deathcore staple.

Fripp NST.desc: Robert Fripp's New Standard Tuning — all fifths (plus a top minor third), built for wide, ringing intervals.

Gambale.desc: Frank Gambale's tuning — the whole guitar up a fourth with the top two strings dropped an octave, so standard shapes yield piano-like close voicings. Invented for his own fusion playing.

Led Rain.desc: Jimmy Page's lush DADGAD variation (a Gsus4/D voicing), written for one specific song.

Blur Song2.desc: Drop D grunge-pop — the low string falls a whole step for the woo-hoo riff's punch.

Schizophrenia.desc: Thurston Moore's clustered Sonic Youth drone tuning — three adjacent scale tones doubled, with no clear root.

Nick Drake.desc: One of Nick Drake's signature open-C-based tunings (capo 2 on the record) — a wide, resonant shimmer.

Keith Richards.desc: Keith's trademark — open G with the low string removed, played on a 5-string.

Am. Football.desc: American Football's open-F(maj9) emo/math-rock tuning — the whole opening line falls under one finger.

SoundG Wave.desc: Chris Cornell & Kim Thayil's drone tuning — often written EEBBBB, but Thayil says it's really EEBBBE.

SoundG Sun.desc: Drop D — the low string falls a whole step; the swaying Leslie-swirl chords ride over it.

Young Cinnamon.desc: Neil Young's crunch tuning — the low string drops a whole step for the riff's growl.

Joni Cab.desc: Joni built her sound on personal open tunings, described by bass note plus fret offsets (her catalog uses 50+).

Joni Sides.desc: Joni's open-D base — a Dmaj7 rings on the open strings. On the record she capos 4 (sounding F# major); this is the no-capo tuning.

Radio Pyramid.desc: Open F# major — let the top F# ring as a pedal while barre shapes slide beneath for the song's swaying, ambiguous chords.

Radio Everything.desc: An "Everything In Its Right Place" voicing built around a C pedal on the top string (the same pedal-note trick as Pyramid Song's F#). Open strings ring C G C G G# C; hold the G → C bender to push the neutral G string up a fourth while the top C keeps ringing.

Mandolin.desc: Standard mandolin, tuned in fifths like a violin.

Irish Bouzouki.desc: The Greek bouzouki adapted for Celtic music — flat-backed, tuned a fifth lower — as a rhythm and countermelody engine.
Irish Bouzouki.song: Irish trad — Planxty (Andy Irvine & Dónal Lunny)

Greek Bouzouki.desc: The bright, tremolo-driven lead of Greek rebetiko and laïkó.

Oud.desc: The fretless lute at the heart of Arabic and Turkish maqam music (tuning varies by region and maqam).
Oud.song: Arabic maqam tradition — e.g. Munir Bashir

Charango.desc: A small Andean lute (traditionally armadillo-shell) with all strings inside one octave — the sparkle of Andean folk.

Saz / Bağlama.desc: Turkey's long-necked folk lute with microtonal, quarter-tone frets — the voice of the âşık poet-minstrels (many regional tunings).

Cavaquinho.desc: A small Brazilian 4-string (open G) — the rhythmic-harmonic engine of samba and choro.

Ukulele.desc: The classic re-entrant soprano/concert uke tuning, with a high g.

Baritone Uke.desc: Tuned like a guitar's top four strings, an octave below a soprano uke — warm and mellow. Favoured in jazz and folk (e.g. Lyle Ritz).

Cuatro.desc: Venezuela's 4-string (re-entrant) — the rhythmic-harmonic base of joropo and música llanera.

Balalaika.desc: Russia's triangular folk lute, played with the fingers.

Sitar.desc: India's long-necked lute with sympathetic strings — here as Sa–Pa drones in C with the Ma melody string on top (Kharaj-Pancham style). The pedals are meend: wide gliding pulls up to a full fifth.

Banjo.desc: A re-entrant 5-string with a high drone — the bluegrass sound.

E9 Nashville.desc: THE country pedal-steel tuning — the crying, gliding sound you picture when you think "pedal steel" (Bud Isaacs, Buddy Emmons).

C6 Swing/Jazz.desc: The "back neck" of a double-neck pedal steel — used for western swing and jazz's fuller chord voicings (Buddy Emmons, Cindy Cashdollar).
C6 Swing/Jazz.song: western swing — Bob Wills; jazz steel — Buddy Emmons

B6 Universal.desc: Jeff Newman's single-neck tuning that fuses the E9 (country) and C6 (jazz/swing) necks, so one neck covers both.

White Keys.desc: The natural notes C D E F G A on six strings — the white-key set every mode is drawn from, with C on the low string as home. Identical to C Ionian.

C Lydian.desc: The brightest mode — major with a raised 4th. Floating, film-score shimmer.

C Ionian.desc: The plain major scale — the mode that feels like home.

C Mixolydian.desc: Major with a flat 7th — the dominant, bluesy-rock colour. (The ♭7 has no open string in this set, so it shares the Ionian shape.)

C Dorian.desc: Minor with a bright natural 6th — the hopeful, funky minor of jazz and modal rock.

C Aeolian.desc: The natural minor scale — ♭3 ♭6 ♭7. The default "sad" minor.

C Phrygian.desc: Minor with a flat 2nd — dark, Spanish/flamenco and metal tension.

C Locrian.desc: The darkest mode — a flat 2nd AND flat 5th give an unstable, diminished tonic.
